FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Garden Bugs & Friends flashcards.

Twenty garden cards for small people who crouch at every flowerpot. Bees, butterflies, worms and a roly-poly or two — with the golden rule baked into every idea: we look, we talk, and the bugs stay where they live.

These cards belong to Toddler 8 on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Look, then look closer

    Show a card, then find the real thing — or a video, or a garden. Say what you both see: stripes, shell, wings. Looking closely is a skill toddlers build fast.

  2. 02

    We look, we do not grab

    Say the rule the same way every time a bug appears: "gentle eyes, gentle hands." Toddlers eventually say it to you — that is how you know it landed.

  3. 03

    Bug hunt on a walk

    Bring two or three cards on a garden walk and match what you find: a bee, a snail, a bird. Real bugs are a bonus, never a requirement.

  4. 04

    Keep hands out of the story

    If your toddler reaches for a bug, offer the card instead: "let's look at the ladybug here." Close looking with safe hands is the whole game.

      Bee Flashcard for Toddlers

      The bee with stripes and buzzy wings, busy on the flowers. Bees are the garden's hardest workers, and toddlers already know the sound before they know the word.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Gives the buzziest neighbour a name before it zooms past the buggy.

      On the next walk

      Carry it to the flowerbeds and wait — a visitor usually arrives within a minute.

      What it teaches

      Links the familiar buzz to its maker, building calm around stinging things.

      Print it like this

      Print on thick card so it survives damp pockets and grass stains.

      Tip for today

      Watch from one step back — bees want flowers, not fingers.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bee lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Garden Bugs & Friends for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      Butterfly Flashcard for Toddlers

      The butterfly with wide painted wings, the prettiest flier in the garden. Butterflies land softly and leave quickly, which makes spotting one feel like a small miracle every time.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Names the garden's shyest flier, the one that never sits still long enough.

      On the next walk

      Walk the flower border slowly and count every butterfly before it flaps off.

      What it teaches

      Builds gentle movement words — flutter, drift, land — plus early counting.

      Print it like this

      Laminate this one — it will be carried everywhere for weeks.

      Tip for today

      Two words are plenty here — pick whichever lands in their day.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Butterfly lesson on the Learning Path.

      Ladybug Flashcard for Toddlers

      The ladybug — tiny, round and spotted, the friendliest beetle in the garden. It fits on a fingertip, which is exactly as close as it needs to get.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Turns the tiniest garden guest into a counting game on legs.

      On the next walk

      Hunt along leaves and walls — every spotted sighting earns a whisper-cheer.

      What it teaches

      Sharpens one-to-one counting on something small enough to hold attention.

      Print it like this

      Two copies print well — one for matching, one for pockets.

      Tip for today

      Spots come in any number — nobody is counting wrong today.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ladybug lesson on the Learning Path.

      Snail Flashcard for Toddlers

      The snail with the curly shell, the slowest walker in the garden and the only one that carries its house. Snails come out when it is damp, which makes rainy days snail days.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Puts slow on the map for a child whose feet only have fast.

      On the next walk

      After rain, patrol the pavement edges — silver trails lead somewhere interesting.

      What it teaches

      Introduces pace as a thing to notice, not just obey.

      Print it like this

      Card stock plus a sleeve keeps it clean for muddy hunts.

      Tip for today

      Bring a magnifying glass — shells reward a closer look.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Snail lesson on the Learning Path.

      Ant Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ants are tiny, busy and everywhere — the picnic's most reliable guests. One ant is easy to miss; a line of ants is a highway your toddler can watch for ages.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Explains the tiny marching line that steals the picnic crumbs.

      On the next walk

      Find a trail on the wall or path and follow it with your eyes.

      What it teaches

      Plants the idea that small workers can do big jobs together.

      Print it like this

      A small print suits this small worker — two to a sheet.

      Tip for today

      Ask where they might all be going — the guesses are gold.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ant lesson on the Learning Path.

      Caterpillar Flashcard for Toddlers

      The caterpillar — long, wiggly and permanently hungry. It is the butterfly's baby, a fact toddlers find astonishing, and it inches along in a way that is irresistible to copy.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Hands over the garden's hungriest wiggle and its famous future trick.

      On the next walk

      Check leaves for nibbled holes — somebody small has been eating here.

      What it teaches

      Stretches the idea of change — today a crawler, someday wings.

      Print it like this

      Full-size is right — the wiggle deserves a big picture.

      Tip for today

      Look, never lift — some fuzzy coats sting, so admire from above.

      Teach it, step by step

      Dragonfly Flashcard for Toddlers

      The dragonfly, zipping over ponds on four glittering wings. It hovers, darts and stops mid-air — the helicopter of the garden, and just as exciting to watch.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Captures the shimmering flier that stops mid-air, then vanishes without warning.

      On the next walk

      Skim the pond edge on your walks and watch the reeds for a hover.

      What it teaches

      Trains quick eyes to follow something fast — genuine visual tracking.

      Print it like this

      Plain white card shows the shiny wings best.

      Tip for today

      Practise the hover at home — arms out, stop dead, hold it.

      Grasshopper Flashcard for Toddlers

      The grasshopper with long jumping legs, hidden in the grass until it leaps. It is the garden's high-jump champion, and its jump is the part toddlers want to replay.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Makes the meadow jumper familiar before you ever hear it click away.

      On the next walk

      Walk the long grass verge and listen for quick rustles, then stop still.

      What it teaches

      Links sound to source, an early listening skill for busy meadows.

      Print it like this

      Print on card and round the corners for pocket trips.

      Tip for today

      Count the leaps you hear — nobody needs to see the jumper.

      Spider Flashcard for Toddlers

      The spider with eight legs, sitting in its web. Spiders make toddlers nervous and grown-ups jump — which is exactly why the calm version belongs on a card first.

      Moth Flashcard for Toddlers

      Print it like this

      Cricket Flashcard for Toddlers

      The cricket, the summer-evening musician. You hear it long before you see it — chirp, chirp, chirp — and finding the singer is a genuine detective game.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Gives the evening chirp an owner your child can point to proudly.

      On the next walk

      Pause on the doorstep after tea and hold a listening contest.

      What it teaches

      Sharpens ears for tiny sounds — the first step to real listening.

      Print it like this

      Keep it by the night light — bedtime material, this one.

      Tip for today

      Describe the sound together — is it jangly, scratchy, chirpy?

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cricket lesson on the Learning Path.

      Roly Poly Flashcard for Toddlers

      The roly-poly — the little grey armadillo bug that curls into a perfect ball when startled. It is the only garden creature with a built-in "again!" button, and toddlers know it.

      Praying Mantis Flashcard for Toddlers

      The praying mantis, standing tall with folded front legs like it is saying grace. It is the garden's stillness champion — it can wait without moving, which makes spotting one feel like winning.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Makes patience look heroic — folded arms, perfect stillness, total focus.

      On the next walk

      Stalk tall stems and flowerbeds slowly — mantises sit tight all morning.

      What it teaches

      Practises standing still on purpose — underrated, difficult, quietly brilliant.

      Print it like this

      Tall format suits it — the posture is the whole point.

      Tip for today

      Quiet contests suit this card — the stillest child wins the day.

      Teach it, step by step

      The centipede — a hundred legs, give or take, rippling along in waves. It moves like nothing else in the garden, and toddlers watch it the way grown-ups watch fireworks.

      Earthworm Flashcard for Toddlers

      The earthworm — pink, wiggly and quietly the most important gardener of all. Worms mix the soil so plants can grow, which makes them the unsung heroes of every flower your toddler has ever smelled.

      Download card ↓

      What this card is for

      Names the wiggle that quietly does the flowerbed's hardest work.

      On the next walk

      Stroll the park path after rain and watch a worm cross the tarmac.

      What it teaches

      Builds kindness for creatures that cannot blink, squeak or thank you.

      Print it like this

      Laminate well — this card loves a rainy walk.

      Tip for today

      Look closely at the segments — counting rings beats touching every time.

      Bird Flashcard for Toddlers

      The garden bird, hopping along the fence, head tilting at everything. Birds are the garden's morning alarm and its loudest regulars — your toddler hears them daily, whether they notice or not.

      Trains stillness and noticing — early listening with a soundtrack.

      Frog Flashcard for Toddlers
